review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped for uses of dyadicHeatGram_coe, cutoffHeatGram_time_congr and dyadic_radius_square_succ across the project (SupportedHeatEnvelope, DyadicHeatAt, DyadicTimeIntegral). I checked the definitions of cutoffHeatGram and cutoffHeatGramEquiv in ActualHeatGrams. The file has no simp attributes at all. The only issue I found is that the unfolding lemma leaves the successor-index time in a non-canonical form, so every caller needs a manual `rw`. I did not find any loop risk or competing rules. I didn't run Lean, so the proposed lemma is untested. I did not recommend making dyadic_radius_square_succ a simp lemma, because its orientation and its fit with other simp normal forms would be questionable.

findings.excerpt: theorem dyadicHeatGram_coe {R lambda : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (i : ℕ) :
findings.problem: The only unfolding lemma for the coerced dyadic Gram is applied by hand, through `simp only [..., dyadicHeatGram_coe]`. For index i+1 it exposes `cutoffHeatGram` at time (R/2^(i+1))^2. The decrement bounds are stated at time (R/2^i)^2/4, so each proof also has to build `hnext` with `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr`, `sq_pos_of_pos`, `div_pos` and `dyadic_radius_square_succ`, then call `rw [hnext]`. The same block is copied in dyadicHeatGram_lower (lines 72-77), dyadicHeatGram_upper (lines 101-105) and SupportedHeatEnvelope (lines 77-80). There is no canonical rewrite from the successor-index Gram to the quarter-time Gram, so simp cannot reach the normal form the downstream lemmas use.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma, say `dyadicHeatGram_succ_coe`. It would say that the coercion of `dyadicHeatGram … (i+1)` equals `cutoffHeatGram … (div_pos (sq_pos_of_pos hs) four_pos) p lambda`, i.e. at time (R/2^i)^2/4. Prove it once with `dyadicHeatGram_coe`, `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr` and `dyadic_radius_square_succ`. Mark `dyadicHeatGram_coe` as `@[simp]` (it is `rfl`, and the right side is a different head symbol, so it cannot loop), and use the succ lemma in the `simp only` calls. The `hnext` boilerplate and the `rw [hnext]` then disappear from all three proofs.
findings.benefit: The time-reindexing step is proved once. The simp set gives a single normal form for the i and i+1 Grams that matches the hypotheses of dyadic_heat_increment_lower_mass and gaussian_dyadic_heat_increment_envelope. Later proofs about the decrement need no ad hoc `rw`.
